basis: Peripheral nerve hyperexcitability causes cramps and fasciculations; these do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Inherited benign fibro-osseous tumors affect bone, particularly the jaws; dental displacement alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Persistent peripheral nerve dysfunction after infection; the residual neuralgia does not itself establish ongoing infection or immune-mediated disease.
Ectodermal defects, deafness and finger contractures define the syndrome; cognitive impairment occurs in 30-79%. Dental disease in 30-79% omitted under the four-axis cap.
Purely psychiatric umbrella without defining damage to an organ axis.
Carcinoma originates in the trachea; regional nodal spread does not establish a separate blood or immune disorder.
Nonsyndromic cochlear hearing loss; bilateral sensorineural impairment reported in 7/7 patients.
Extensive myelomeningocele affects spinal neural tissue and vertebral closure; neurogenic bladder with loss of urinary function occurs in over 80% of myelomeningocele patients.
Cold-triggered mast-cell-mediated urticaria defines a skin and immune-mediated disorder; systemic reactions do not establish lasting additional organ damage.
Malignant soft-tissue tumor with skeletal muscle differentiation, usually arising in deep extremity tissues.
Defined by structural or functional disease of arteries; downstream organ injury is not uniform across this umbrella.
Oocyte maturation failure and infertility affect reproductive cells without evidence of gonadal endocrine dysfunction.
Deep soft-tissue adipocytic sarcoma, usually retroperitoneal; its inflammatory infiltrate does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Destructive xanthogranulomatous inflammation affects salivary glands; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Inherited defects of neurotransmitter synthesis, metabolism or transport directly impair nervous-system function.
Fungal infection defined by its organism; no single anatomical site applies across localized and invasive presentations.
Glaucoma-spectrum ocular condition; borderline status does not establish damage outside the eye.
Retinal degeneration and renal ciliopathy are central recessive IFT140 manifestations; skeletal dysplasia varies by subtype and is not assigned across the umbrella.
Retinal dystrophy, cataracts, intellectual disability and short stature define the syndrome; brachydactyly occurs in 30-79%. Dental malocclusion affects 3/3 patients.
Retinal degeneration, hearing loss and Fanconi renal dysfunction define the syndrome; phosphate-wasting rickets affects 4/6 patients.
The available concept identifies ectodermal dysplasia with blindness; no evidence supports additional organ axes.
Bladder evagination and pelvic, pelvic-floor and abdominal-wall defects define the condition. Anal positional anomalies alone do not establish bowel damage; UTIs are separate infections.
Benign blood-vessel tumor arising in the dermis and subcutis.
Cherubism replaces jaw bone with cyst-like lesions; optic atrophy causes visual impairment. Optic nerve disease is assigned to the ocular axis.
Defined by progressive loss of central nervous system tissue and neurological function; other organ damage is not shared across the umbrella.
